note: Four Upgrade Roadmap 2 livestock-lifecycle systems. Existing workbook numbers are unchanged. Reference quantities and game assumptions are distinguished in row notes.

systems.name: Egg Incubator (24 eggs)
systems.description: Hatch your own flock's eggs into chicks; needs steady electricity for 21 days.
systems.notes: Batch: 24 eggs from stock + 0.5 kWh/day for 21 days -> about 70% hatch as Baby Chicks (LL-31 cohort). Chicken eggs hatch in about 21 days: https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/animal_husbandry/ani_chik_hatching%20of%20eggs.html ; hatch rate, power draw and the two-missed-day tolerance are experimental game assumptions. Needs a mature laying flock on the parcel (fertile eggs). Eggs and electricity are drawn per batch, not as steady weekly flows.

systems.name: Broody Hen Nest Box
systems.description: Let a broody hen hatch a clutch in spring and summer; she stops laying while she sits.
systems.notes: Batch: 8 eggs from stock under one hen from a mature flock within 30 ft, 21 days -> about 85% hatch as Baby Chicks. A standard hen covers about 6-12 eggs: https://www.hobbyfarms.com/how-to-work-with-a-broody-hen/ ; broodiness limited to days with at least 13 h daylight. Hatch rate, range and daylight threshold are experimental game assumptions.

systems.name: Predator-Proof Run (12 birds)
systems.description: A roofed, buried-wire run that keeps up to 12 birds nearby safe from predators.
systems.notes: Protects up to 12 lifecycle poultry within 20 ft from LL-31 predator losses while staffed (80% upkeep met). Lumber frame plus hardware cloth; 150 lb lumber is a game assumption. Capacity, range and costs are experimental game balance.

systems.name: Rotational Paddock Kit
systems.description: Portable fencing to rest and rotate a pasture; raises its hay and green biomass when moved weekly.
systems.notes: Place on a pasture: its Hay and Green biomass output x up to 1.15, scaled by how much of the 1 h/week moving labor was done. Evidence is mixed: UF/IFAS reports more forage under rotation on bahiagrass https://rcrec-ona.ifas.ufl.edu/news-and-publications/in-focus-archives/forage/grazing-methods-impact-on-forage-cattle-production/ while a rangeland review found continuous grazing equal or better in most experiments https://bioone.org/journals/rangeland-ecology-and-management/volume-61/issue-1/06-159R.1/Rotational-Grazing-on-Rangelands--Reconciliation-of-Perception-and-Experimental/10.2111/06-159R.1.full ; the 15% bonus is a conservative game assumption.
